question: Which statement best describes The document frame?
options: `About us` creates a link to a page on the same site. The `href` value is the destination, and the text is what people activate. It is like a sign with both a direction and a readable label. The destination should work when opened directly too. For example, use `/account` for a route on the same site and a full URL for a different site. In practice, use a fragment link to jump to a heading whose ID remains unique on the page.

A URL can be a full address such as `https://example.com` or a path such as `/about`. A path stays within the current site. It is like using a street address or a room number in the same building. Choose the form that matches whether the destination is internal or external. For example, a link to `#pricing` works when the page contains a matching unique element ID. In practice, give repeated navigation links enough context to distinguish their destinations.

A fragment such as `#contact` jumps to an element whose `id` is `contact`. It is like a bookmark inside a long document. Use a unique ID and make sure the destination heading is visible after the jump, especially when a fixed header could cover it. For example, write “Read the refund policy” when that is the link destination. In practice, a download link should name the file or explain what will be downloaded.

Descriptive link text tells people what will happen, such as “Read the return policy.” It is like labeling a sign with the destination instead of “go there.” Avoid vague text such as “click here,” which is difficult to understand when links are read out of context. For example, use a button to submit a form; use a link to open a destination. In practice, use rel protection when opening an external destination in a new tab.
explanation: `About us` creates a link to a page on the same site. The `href` value is the destination, and the text is what people activate. It is like a sign with both a direction and a readable label. The destination should work when opened directly too. For example, use `/account` for a route on the same site and a full URL for a different site. In practice, use a fragment link to jump to a heading whose ID remains unique on the page.

Opening a new tab changes browser behavior and can disorient people. Use it only when there is a clear reason, and explain the behavior when it may surprise someone. It is like opening a second book without closing the first. Native links preserve expected keyboard and browser actions. For example, if a new tab is necessary, make that behavior clear to the person activating the link. In practice, verify a route works after refresh, not only after client-side navigation.
